card.name: Ura
card.era: pre-colonial Polynesian; modern hip-isolation style codified c.1970
card.tagline: Cook Islands drum dance that tells stories with the hips
card.profile: The 'ura is the traditional dance of the Cook Islands (Polynesia), most famously the 'ura pa'u or drum dance set to fast, layered rhythms from a full ensemble of drums (pate, tokere, pa'u). Per Wikipedia, women move the hips, legs and hands to narrate stories of the ocean, birds, flowers, love and sadness, while men flap their knees in a semi-crouch holding the upper body steady; dancers wear pareu and kikau (grass) skirts with 'ei flower and shell garlands. It belongs to a family including Tahitian 'ote'a and Hawaiian hula.
card.insight: 'Ura is the centrepiece of Cook Islands cultural identity, celebrated annually at the Te Mire Ura (Dancer of the Year) competition, and Cook Islanders are widely regarded among Polynesia's finest drummers and dancers (Wikipedia; Te Papa).
